observations:
Torah LM2 #87 is an exceptionally compact teaching (9 lines). The Rebbe states only two explicit bechina identifications: (1) isha=derech and (2) yam=emunah. These two pairs form the two packages already identified. There is no third conceptual cluster of 3+ bechina-connected nodes in the source text that would warrant a new package.

All remaining concepts in the Torah are connected by eitza (cause-and-effect) relationships: kavvanat Elul → tikkun habrit → finding one's zivug. These are directional flow relationships, not parallel-nature bechinas. They belong to the causal narrative structure of the teaching, not to package formation.

The narrative elements (Avraham, Eliezer, Yitzchak, the verse 've'im lo tove ha'isha lalekhet acharecha,' the acrostic spelling of Elul) are illustrative proof-texts and story references, not bechina-identified concepts. The Rebbe treats them as examples and evidence, not as concepts sharing the same essential nature as other nodes.

The concept of 'kavvanat Elul' itself — while central to the Torah — is connected to 'tikkun habrit' via eitza, not bechina. The kavvanot cause the tikkun; they are not identified as sharing the same essential nature as the tikkun. Similarly, 'tikkun habrit' is connected to 'finding one's zivug' via eitza.

Conclusion: the two packages (אשה/דרך and ים/אמונה) represent the complete bechina topology of this Torah. No new packages are needed.
